activities.title: Four word classes, four jobs
activities.instructions: Start here. In class, discuss the examples with a partner. Studying alone, say your answers aloud before moving on.
activities.content:
GOALS
By the end, you can name the job a word does, use nearby words to choose its form, and explain your choice in a workplace sentence. Allow 35–45 minutes for all ten activities.

WARM-UP
“The assistant organized the files quickly.” Which word names a person? Which expresses the action? Which tells you how the action happened?

NOUN: a person, thing or idea — assistant, file, efficiency.
VERB: an action or state — organize, work, seem.
ADJECTIVE: describes a noun or follows a linking verb — an efficient assistant; the assistant is efficient.
ADVERB: modifies a verb, adjective or another adverb — works efficiently; extremely efficient.

Warm-up check: assistant = noun; organized = verb; quickly = adverb. Meaning helps, but the word’s position gives you a useful grammar clue.

activities.title: Read a workplace update
activities.instructions: Read the original memo. Find a noun, a verb, an adjective and an adverb. Then compare your choices with the worked examples.
activities.content:
TEAM UPDATE
Our efficient assistant organized the new files yesterday. She checked every folder carefully. Her careful review improved the accuracy of the records. The system now works efficiently.

WORKED EXAMPLES
“assistant” is a noun: it names the person doing the work.
“organized” is a verb: it tells us what the assistant did.
“efficient” is an adjective: it describes assistant.
“carefully” is an adverb: it describes how she checked.
“accuracy” is a noun: it names the quality that improved.

WORD FAMILY
efficiency (noun) → efficient (adjective) → efficiently (adverb). Do not pick a form just because you recognize its meaning: choose the form that fits its job.

Notice: careful describes the noun review, while carefully describes the verb checked. A word ending can help, but it is not proof: friendly is usually an adjective, and fast can be an adjective or an adverb.

activities.title: Identify the word class
activities.instructions: In the sentence “The manager spoke confidently,” what kind of word is confidently?
activities.content: Choose the word class that best describes “confidently.”
activities.explanation: Confidently tells us how the manager spoke, so it modifies the verb and is an adverb. Manager is the noun and spoke is the verb. An adjective would describe the manager: “The confident manager spoke.”

activities.title: Choose the correct form
activities.instructions: Choose the best word to complete the sentence.
activities.content: Our customer service team responds ______ to all inquiries.
activities.explanation: Promptly is the adverb describing how the team responds. Prompt is an adjective (“a prompt reply”); promptness is a noun (“their promptness”); prompted is a verb form. The blank modifies responds, so promptly fits.

activities.title: Complete the sentence
activities.instructions: Type the correct form of the word in brackets.
activities.content: The new scheduling software has improved office ______. (efficient)
activities.explanation: Efficiency is the noun naming what has improved. Office modifies that noun. Efficient is an adjective and efficiently is an adverb; neither can serve as the object of improved here. The complete phrase is “improved office efficiency.”

activities.title: TOEIC sentence completion
activities.instructions: Select the option that makes the sentence grammatically correct.
activities.content: Employees must obtain written ______ before purchasing new equipment.
activities.explanation: Approval is a noun and is the object of obtain; written describes that noun. Approve is a verb, approved is a past-tense/participle form, and approvingly is an adverb. Use the position clue: obtain + adjective + noun.

activities.title: Repair the error
activities.instructions: Rewrite the incorrect word in its correct form.
activities.content: The board was complete satisfied with the quarterly results. Which word should replace “complete”?
activities.explanation: Completely is the adverb modifying the adjective satisfied. Complete is an adjective, which can describe a noun (“a complete report”) but cannot modify satisfied here. The corrected sentence is “The board was completely satisfied with the quarterly results.”

activities.title: Review the clues, avoid the traps
activities.instructions: Pause and explain one rule using your own example. In class, share it with a partner. Alone, write or say a sentence before continuing.
activities.content:
A FOUR-STEP CHECK
1. Read the whole sentence for meaning.
2. Find the words immediately before and after the blank.
3. Decide the job: noun, verb, adjective or adverb.
4. Choose the form and read the completed sentence again.

POSITION CLUES
Article + adjective + noun: “an efficient team.”
Verb + noun object: “improve efficiency.”
Adverb + adjective: “extremely efficient.”
Verb + adverb: “work efficiently.”
Linking verb + adjective: “The team seems efficient.”

COMMON TRAPS
An article does not always sit directly before a noun: an extremely efficient team is also correct.
Not every -ly word is an adverb: a friendly colleague uses an adjective.
After be or seem, describe the subject: “The report is complete,” not “The report is completely.”

SELF-CHECK
Explain the difference between “a careful review” and “review carefully.” Answer: careful describes the noun review; carefully describes the action review.

activities.title: Short quiz
activities.instructions: Final check: choose the form that fits, then explain which word the blank describes.
activities.content: The marketing department created an extremely ______ campaign.
activities.explanation: Effective is the adjective describing the noun campaign. Extremely is an adverb modifying effective. Effect and effectiveness are nouns; effectively is an adverb. The pattern is adverb + adjective + noun: “an extremely effective campaign.”

activities.title: Unit review and next practice
activities.instructions: Review the six scored answers and their explanations. In self-study, mark this final activity complete to see your first-attempt score.
activities.content:
CAN YOU DO THESE THREE THINGS?
• Identify the job a word performs in a sentence.
• Use the position of a blank to choose a word form.
• Explain why an answer fits instead of relying only on its ending.

RETRIEVAL CHECK
Without looking back, name the noun, adjective and adverb in this family: efficiency → efficient → efficiently. Make a new workplace sentence using each form.

EXAMPLE ANSWERS
“The new system improves efficiency.”
“We have an efficient team.”
“The team works efficiently.”

WHAT TO DO NEXT
If you missed a question, revisit its explanation and name the position clue. If you answered all six correctly, write two original sentences that contrast an adjective and an adverb.

In class, share one sentence and explain your choice before the teacher ends the session. Outside class, complete the unit in self-study to save your own learning record. Class responses and self-study progress are separate practice records.

activities.instructions: Prepare, then speak for 30 seconds without reading.
activities.content: Introduce yourself, say what you study or do, and describe one reason you are learning English.

activities.title: The sentence core
activities.instructions: Find the subject and the main verb in each example.
activities.content: A complete English sentence normally needs a subject and a finite verb: “The class starts.” Extra information can be added after this reliable core.
